title: Optimize Console: actionable batching & cache recommendation workflows with safe-apply UI
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Build a coherent Optimize Console workflow that surfaces model-specific batching and KV/prefix-cache recommendations as first-class recommendation cards, lets operators preview exact configuration diffs, run safe applies (dry-run, canary, staged rollouts) and provides a searchable apply-history / audit trail with who/when/why metadata. Goal is to reduce token/unit spend by surfacing high-confidence changes while preserving SLOs and enabling rapid rollback and auditability for enterprise customers.
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to see prioritized recommendation cards per route/model so I can decide which suggestions to apply to reduce cost without degrading latency.
As a platform engineer, I want to preview the exact JSON/YAML config diff that will be applied so I can validate it against infra constraints before rollout.
As an ops lead, I want a canary/staged rollout option that applies a change to 5% of traffic and auto-rolls back on SLA regressions so we can safely test cost optimizations.
As a security reviewer, I want an immutable apply history with user identity, timestamp, and links to evaluation snapshots so audits are straightforward.
As a product PM, I want to measure actual cost delta and quality regressions (per-variant) after recommendations are applied so we can refine recommendation heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display: model, route, estimated monthly cost savings, confidence score, estimated latency impact, and recommended config snippet.
Diff preview UI renders a syntactic diff of the current runtime config vs proposed config and allows toggling between JSON/YAML and human readable summary.
Safe-apply options include: Dry-run (no service change), Canary (% traffic), Staged rollout (by region/route), and Immediate apply with rollback button available.
Apply-history is queryable by user, model, route, and date; each record includes actor (SSO identity), timestamp, diff link, pre/post snapshots, and optional comment reason.
System supports automatic rollback triggers based on pre-defined SLO regressions (error rate, p95 latency) and records the trigger in the audit entry.
Changes pushed via Optimize are emitted to infra events stream and generate a GitOps-style commit id for reconciliation with Dedicated/Private deployments.
Security review documented and compliant with KMS/RBAC constraints for Private customers; feature toggles exist to restrict auto-apply to enterprise orgs only.
engineering_notes: Core work split across three eng areas: recommendation service (algorithms + CI for confidence scoring), console UX for the cards/diff/flows, and runtime apply/rollback plumbing. Runtime team must expose an idempotent apply API that accepts 'dry-run' and 'canary' modes and returns pre/post snapshots. We plan to re-use existing audit-log pipeline (ENG-3702) and extend event schema with 'optimize.apply' verb. Quantization/batching suggestions must include validation harness that runs synthetic load to estimate latency impact. Trade-offs: start with read-only diff preview for GA, enable auto-apply only for customers who opt-in; restrict auto-apply to Dedicated and Hosted with enterprise opt-in for Private initially.
rollout_plan: Phase A (2 weeks): read-only recommendation cards + diff preview + SSO-protected 'request change' flow. Phase B (3 weeks): dry-run and canary apply via runtime API + dashboarding for canary telemetry. Phase C (2 weeks): staged rollout & auto-rollback rules + apply-history UI and exports. Gate: security review and infra reliability sign-off required before Phase B. Phased launch starts with internal Redwood org, then a closed beta with 3 enterprise customers, then general availability.
audit_and_rollback: Each apply generates an immutable audit entry containing actor (SSO), commit id, config diff, associated evaluation snapshot id, canary config, and autoscale snapshot. Automatic rollback engine listens to canary telemetry and will execute runtime rollback with a reason code and write a follow-up audit entry. Manual rollback button in console allows SRE to revert to latest prior commit. All audit entries are retained for 2 years and exportable via CSV/JSON for compliance teams.
qa_plan: End-to-end tests for diff rendering, unit tests for diff generation, integration tests for runtime dry-run and canary APIs, chaos-tests that trigger rollback, and UX validation with accessibility checks. Create a test org in staging with synthetic workloads to validate cost savings and no SLO regressions. Add regression alerts tied to 'optimize.apply' events.
metrics: median estimated vs actual cost delta (30d)
percent of canaries that rolled back
